title: EffectSlice: Source-Grounded Certificates for Task-Local Paper Effects
hook: EffectSlice defines a paper's core innovation on one locked task as the smallest source-anchored procedural slice whose paired net effect is statistically equivalent to the complete PaperToSkill artifact. Unlike semantic or dependency-only compression, every retained and deleted procedure carries an effect-preservation certificate against the same no-skill scaffold.
hook_shape_rationale: We use counter-intuitive minimalism: relative to the complete PaperToSkill artifact, EffectSlice executes a strict procedural subset while preserving the same task-local paired net effect within a preregistered equivalence margin. A surprising empirical reveal was rejected because the contribution is the certified object and compiler, not a result inferred from the eight known development tasks.

gap_closure.gap: Under a limited initial budget, no retrieved frontier establishes that the observed low-fidelity score preserves the sign and ordering of paper interventions by the performance improvement they later produce on independently specified user tasks; a probe can therefore support the wrong go/no-go decision even when it is internally faithful.
gap_closure.how_closed: The opaque notion of a paper's core innovation is reformulated as a source-grounded constrained subset object whose faithfulness criterion is direct equivalence to the complete artifact's paired net effect on the same locked task.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier estimates net benefit after execution cost, adaptation effort, and regressions on task dimensions outside the paper's headline metric are deducted from gross performance gain.
gap_closure.how_closed: The complete artifact is replaced only by a compact executable slice whose simultaneous effect-gap interval lies inside the preregistered margin, whose contract and guardrails remain noninferior, and whose measured task-local execution and adaptation costs are lower.

core_mechanism: For one paper p and one locked user task tau, EffectSlice preregisters cases x_i, case weights w_i, paired seeds, a no-skill same-scaffold baseline B, the complete PaperToSkill artifact F, primary scorer m in [0,1], guardrail scorers r_j in [0,1], cost weights lambda_gpu, lambda_api, and lambda_labor, effect-equivalence margin epsilon, guardrail margins eta_j, familywise error alpha, and a maximum adaptive query budget Q. The source map defines procedural atoms P, each with a paper-span anchor, executable file or instruction span, dependency edges, and a task-contract role; a candidate S must be source-valid, dependency-closed, executable, and contract-passing before effect evidence is considered. For any artifact A in {F,S}, paired case-seed outcome z_ir(A) equals m(y_ir(A))-m(y_ir(B)) minus the declared GPU, API, labor, and guardrail-regression penalties relative to B, and Delta_tau(A) is the preregistered weighted mean of z_ir(A). The new object is Cert_tau(S): source anchors and hashes, the paired effect gap G_tau(S)=Delta_tau(S)-Delta_tau(F), an anytime-valid confidence sequence I_tau(S) for G_tau(S), contract and guardrail verdicts, and the complete adaptive query log. Candidate q spends preregistered alpha_q with sum_q alpha_q at most alpha, uses the same case-seed pairing for S, F, and B, and is effect-preserving only when I_tau(S) is wholly inside [-epsilon,epsilon], every contract passes, and each guardrail difference r_j(S)-r_j(F) is at least -eta_j. The fixed-length vector of paired per-case effect differences is the compact intermediate to which verification is attached; its confidence radius R_tau(S) is independent of the number of source procedures and directly bounds the property the substitute must preserve. The compiler may use delta debugging, program slicing, subset selection, or any other search backend, but those procedures are explicitly interchangeable and not claimed as novel; acceptance is determined only by Cert_tau(S). To handle non-monotone obligation interactions, the default backend searches source-consistent dependency blocks, keeps an accepted-subset frontier, re-enqueues every previously rejected block after an accepted deletion, tests pairwise unions in the changed dependency neighborhood, and finishes with a complete one-deletion scan under the remaining query budget. Construction-time source, contract, or guardrail failures return typed feedback that restores missing prerequisites or repairs only the invalid adapter before the candidate is re-evaluated; effect-equivalence failures are never repaired by changing epsilon or the scorer. The output S_star is one-deletion-minimal: Cert_tau(S_star) passes, while for every retained atom o, S_star without o fails effect equivalence, contract, or guardrail noninferiority; final certificates are re-estimated on sealed confirmation pairs with Holm correction across S_star and all retained-atom deletions, each deleted atom stores the accepted transition certificate that removed it and a final source-grounded absence trace, each retained atom stores the failed-removal certificate naming the violated condition, and the result is task-local and never pooled into a cross-paper model or transported to another task.
core_mechanism_reasoning: The two gaps share Cert_tau(S): C00 makes the paper's task-local core a precise constrained effect-preservation object, and C09 makes the certified slice a runnable substitute for the costly complete artifact. I considered ordinary delta debugging, dynamic slicing, ablation, subset selection, and factorial search, but rejected all of them as contribution claims; they remain replaceable search implementations and explicit baselines, while novelty is restricted to the source-grounded effect-preservation certificate and compiler contract. This avoids lineage nodes n1 and c1-c4 because EffectSlice estimates no cheap-to-later bridge, common fidelity curve, cross-paper selector, or source-to-target extrapolation.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Freeze the task manifest before compilation; input is one locked task's cases, scorers, paired seeds, cost weights, epsilon, eta_j, alpha, and Q, and output is an immutable certification specification.
2. Materialize F and the same-scaffold no-skill baseline B under identical model, tools, environment, cache, and caps; input is the current PaperToSkill artifact and output is two executable reference branches.
3. Parse the source map into source-anchored procedural atoms and dependency blocks, resolve every paper span and file reference, and emit P plus a typed dependency and contract graph.
4. Run paired F and B references on the preregistered case-seed pairs; input is the task manifest and output is Delta_tau(F), reference guardrails, costs, and immutable run hashes.
5. Initialize S as P and ask an interchangeable search backend for source-consistent single or block deletions; input is the current accepted frontier and output is a candidate S' plus its exact atom diff.
6. Compile S' during construction, feeding source, dependency, contract, and guardrail-check failures back to restore a missing prerequisite or repair only the invalid adapter; output is a runnable candidate or a typed rejection.
7. Execute runnable S' against B on the same paired cases and seeds, compute G_tau(S'), and update its anytime-valid confidence sequence using alpha_q from the preregistered spending schedule; output is Cert_tau(S').
8. Accept S' only when its effect-gap interval is inside [-epsilon,epsilon], contracts pass, and all guardrails are noninferior; otherwise retain S and record the exact failed condition without changing margins.
9. After every accepted deletion, revisit rejected blocks, test pairwise unions in the changed dependency neighborhood, and maintain multiple accepted subsets when effects are non-monotone; input is the query history and output is an interaction-aware accepted frontier.
10. At query completion, run every remaining one-atom deletion from the best accepted slice and use sealed confirmation pairs with Holm correction to certify S_star and each retained atom's failed deletion.
11. Emit S_star, executable files, Cert_tau(S_star), retained-atom failed-removal certificates, and deleted-atom accepted-transition certificates; report Delta_tau(S_star), Delta_tau(F), guardrails, and local costs for this task only.
12. Evaluate the frozen compiler on genuinely new paper-task pairs, comparing semantic top-k, size-matched random or truncation, dependency-only closure, manual operator ablation, and interchangeable delta-debugging backends under identical task-local budgets.
falsification_prediction: After using the existing eight tasks only for compiler development and replay, freeze atomization, search, epsilon, eta_j, Q, and alpha spending, then acquire at least four genuinely new paper-task pairs whose task assets, scorers, source maps, and complete artifacts were not used to design the compiler; run EffectSlice and semantic top-k, size-matched random or truncation, dependency-only closure, and manual operator-ablation baselines under the same paired budget, reporting each task separately. If the mechanism works, each held-out S_star will have a sealed paired confidence interval for Delta_tau(S_star)-Delta_tau(F) wholly inside [-epsilon,epsilon], no contract or guardrail failure, and lower executed-procedure count and local cost than F, while the matched baselines fail effect equivalence on more of the same task-local comparisons. The single load-bearing variable is the certified effect-gap radius R_tau(S), the simultaneous upper confidence radius used to decide whether a slice preserves the complete artifact's effect. As a negative control, permute R_tau labels across contract-passing same-size candidate slices before selection; on untouched confirmation pairs, the selected slice's paired net effect should move toward the no-skill baseline and its effect gap should leave the equivalence margin, matching semantic or random selection rather than EffectSlice.
compute_budget: Full campaign with eight development replays and at least four genuinely new held-out task cases: approximately 36 GPU-days on 80GB-class GPUs plus about $5,000 in paid API inference for complete-artifact references, adaptive paired queries, sealed confirmation runs, interaction revisits, and matched baselines; feasible within the stated 50 GPU-day and bounded-API envelope.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: That framework generates tasks from a skill and estimates whole-skill marginal utility, whereas EffectSlice starts from an independently locked task and certifies the smallest source-anchored procedural subset whose paired net effect is equivalent to the complete artifact against the same no-skill baseline.

PaperBench's requirement hierarchy scores completeness of complete and code-only replication, whereas EffectSlice makes task-local effect equivalence to the complete artifact the acceptance condition and emits retained and deleted procedure certificates.

AutoReproduce uses lineage evidence, mini-batch checks, and dry runs to construct an end-to-end reproduction, whereas EffectSlice treats that complete artifact as a reference and compiles a smaller source-grounded slice only when paired net effect, contracts, and guardrails are preserved.

SkillFoundry accepts skills after execution, system, and synthetic contract tests, whereas EffectSlice requires a simultaneous task-local effect-gap certificate against the complete artifact and assigns a failed-removal or accepted-deletion effect certificate to every procedure atom.

what_step_was_missed: It would have needed to keep the user's task fixed, use the complete artifact and no-skill scaffold as paired references, atomize the artifact by source provenance, and certify a one-deletion-minimal subset by simultaneous effect-equivalence, contract, and guardrail constraints.
